findings.title: Predecessor clean v2 reviews survive the tracked-parent correction
findings.diagnosis: A predecessor snapshot follows a symlink replacing an internal tracked directory and reports a clean tree. Its review uses hma.host.review-artifact/v2 with an empty worktree field. Restoring a real directory with equal tracked bytes yields the same current clean head/diff and review identity. The CLI accepts the old independent review and appends IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW -> VERIFICATION. The v8 worktree domain only retires dirty identities; it cannot invalidate the empty clean worktree identity.

evidence.observation: legacy-clean-parent/bind=false reconstructs predecessor clean observation, restores a real directory, and accepts the full transition; store gains a Verification transition. The test fails the required refusal.
The second requested binding branch repeats the accepted legacy clean replay. Its optional worktree binding is empty because the observation is clean.
ReviewArtifactDigest still uses hma.host.review-artifact/v2 for both clean and dirty observations.
The changed hma-worktree-v8 domain is used only when Snapshot reports dirty content.
24 of 26 full artifact subcases pass. Fresh clean and dirty controls pass. Current byte/mode/type/index/ignore/case changes and reconstructed predecessor v7 dirty reviews refuse.

fix.action: Retire the predecessor clean review domain in internal/host/host.go, for example by advancing ReviewArtifactDigest to hma.host.review-artifact/v3 after the parent-component correction. Require fresh independent review records using the new domain for clean and dirty artifacts. Add an actual predecessor clean-v2 replay regression.
fix.why: The old clean review record has no observation-version binding outside the artifact schema. Changing the dirty-worktree digest cannot revoke that authority.

verification.method: Rerun TestAuditorR6FullArtifactMatrix legacy-clean-parent against a helper that preserves the predecessor v2 artifact schema. Do not recompute historical review records with the new digest function.
verification.expected: Both clean predecessor replay branches refuse with no core/host record or head byte changes.

verification.method: Record a fresh review of the supported real-directory checkout and present a fresh valid human approval. Repeat dirty controls with the optional worktree field absent and populated.
verification.expected: Current unchanged clean and dirty controls advance; all changed artifacts and historical clean/dirty identities refuse.

verification.method: Repeat package test, vet, race, dogfood and affected independent artifact probes on the frozen corrected target.
verification.expected: All mandatory checks pass; no stale review authorizes Verification.

fix.tradeoffs: A schema bump invalidates all predecessor v2 reviews, including valid ones. They need a fresh independent review and a fresh approval when the new review changes the core binding context. Store history remains append-only. No patch has been applied or validated.
fix.alternative: Persist and check an explicit snapshot-observation version in the immutable review artifact contract. This gives a durable migration boundary but is a larger record/compatibility change. There is no safe way to distinguish valid and incomplete old clean v2 observations from their head/diff/empty-worktree values alone.

limitations: Fresh session with only the user dispatch and neutral/authoritative requirement sources. No implementer conversation or earlier Gate B reviews were read. Source comments, implementation tests and the changed Task 14 document were inspected as artifacts; their explanations are not proof.

Read-only by conduct and unchanged final source freeze, not an OS-enforced read-only mount. All persistent audit artifacts and caches are under this output directory. Independent Go probes also used automatically removed default /tmp/Test... fixture directories. The dogfood harness created and removed its /tmp scratch store. No source files or Git state were written.

Linux/amd64, Go 1.27.1. No Windows, macOS, case-insensitive filesystem, actual power cut, or hosted GitHub Actions run. Filesystem model assumes successful file fsync persists file data, and models loss of unsynchronized directory entries. It tests the all-loss image and ordinary process restart at each checkpoint, not every arbitrary subset/reordering or physical device behavior.

The precise earlier named probe scripts and their 40/55 checkpoints were not read or executed because earlier review directories were withheld. Independent equivalent probes were built instead; 51 first-append, 89 successor and 101 recovery checkpoint runs passed. Initial malformed auditor test files failed to compile before correction; those setup failures are not product defects. Final probe logs contain corrected executions. Initial auditor-only compile errors remain in the session tool trace.

Initial test and race runs failed one test because the test assumed its repository source directory lay outside os.TempDir. Reruns of the untouched source copy with TMPDIR set to a dedicated scratch directory passed. The initial failures remain in test.log and race.log.

The predecessor helper reconstructs only the specified v7 behavior: old raw leaf Lstat that follows parent symlinks, and worktree domain v7. No earlier implementation tree or earlier review packet was read. This is an executable controlled reconstruction, not an authenticated historical binary.

Clean observations have an empty Worktree digest. The legacy-clean reproduction runs both requested binding branches, but both have an absent serialized optional WorktreeDigest. Populated dirty binding cases are separate and pass.

Exact worker/model/effort route was supplied by the dispatch as liz/gpt-6.1-sol/high. The host does not expose a separate cryptographic runtime model attestation. No subagent, nested agent CLI, model API, external messages, git writes, or source edits were used.
Jev is unavailable in the exposed host tool inventory. The auditor used the orchestrator decision fallback. No Jev result was fabricated.
F05, C04 and R3-03 are PARTIAL but nonmandatory for Gate B under the supplied human scope decision. This audit does not claim full host MVP conformance or release readiness.
